example.title: Branch River Bridge, Main Street (NH Route 12) over the Branch River (Otter Brook)

brief: Two-span continuous reinforced-concrete T-beam bridge on a city main street, built 1935 in a Public Works road-widening: 122 ft long with two 54.5 ft clear spans, beams of variable depth with a curved outer fascia sweeping down to the central pier, cantilever abutments on timber piles with square-return wingwalls, 14 ft clearance over the river. Overall width 34 ft 4 in with a 24 ft asphalt roadway between curbs and a concrete sidewalk each side; the original concrete guard rail is an open parapet of short rectangular openings between posts, with plain end blocks. Street lights on tall poles, overhead wires and a BRIDGE / weight sign at the ends; bare riverbank trees below.
